info.name: Cookies without HttpOnly attribute - Detect
author: rj coleman
mr.bobo hp
info.description: Checks whether cookies in the HTTP response contain the HttpOnly attribute. If the HttpOnly flag is set, it means that the cookie is HTTP-only
info.impact: Lack of HttpOnly flag on cookies increases the risk of client-side attacks, compromising user session security and data privacy.
info.remediation: Ensure that all cookies are set with the HttpOnly attribute to prevent client-side access.

info.name: vsftpd <= 3.0.2 - Access Restriction Bypass
author: pussycat0x
info.description: vsftpd 3.0.2 and earlier contain a vulnerability that allows remote attackers to bypass access restrictions due to improper parsing of the deny_file configuration directive.
info.impact: Unauthenticated attackers can bypass access restrictions configured via the deny_file directive to access files that should be restricted, potentially exposing sensitive data on vsftpd servers.
info.remediation: Update vsftpd to a version newer than 3.0.2 that properly parses and enforces the deny_file configuration directive to prevent access restriction bypass.

info.name: vsftpd < 3.0.3 - DoS
author: pussycat0x
info.description: vsftpd before 3.0.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service by sending a crafted FTP command.
info.impact: Attackers can send crafted FTP commands to crash the vsftpd daemon, causing denial of service and interrupting FTP services for legitimate users.
info.remediation: Upgrade to vsftpd version 3.0.3 or later that addresses the denial of service vulnerability.

info.name: DVWA Exposed Setup Page
author: mayoubmalik1-blip
info.description: A Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) setup page is exposed. An unauthenticated attacker can use the setup page to reset the database, which restores the default credentials (admin:password), and the page discloses database configuration details.

Database Setup

You can also use this to reset the administrator credentials ("admin // password") at any stage.
